Archive item 1: Western Corridor Maintenance Program – Budget Allocation Memo
Source format: budget allocation memo

This category covers rail grinding, resurfacing, and tamping activities across the corridor. It includes material costs for ballast, sleepers, and fastenings, as well as the engagement of specialist track maintenance crews. Planned activities include the replacement of 12 kilometres of rail on the Ballan–Gordon section and targeted sleeper renewal at known defect locations identified in the 2025 asset condition assessment.

**3.2 Signalling & Communications (WCMP-SIG) – $720,000**

Funding in this category supports the upgrade of level crossing warning systems at three priority sites: Dunnstown Road, Learmonth Street, and the Waubra crossing. The allocation also covers routine maintenance of the existing signalling network and the replacement of obsolete communications equipment at the Ballan control point.

**3.3 Civil Works & Structures (WCMP-CIV) – $1,050,000**

This category funds drainage improvements, culvert repairs, and bridge inspection and maintenance works. Key activities include the replacement of the timber deck on the Burrumbeet Creek bridge and concrete repair works at the Creswick Road overpass. A provision is included for emergency stabilisation works should they be required following the spring inspection programme.

**3.4 Plant & Equipment Hire (WCMP-PLT) – $480,000**

This allocation covers the hire of track maintenance machinery, including tampers, regulators, and rail grinders, as well as the operation of hi-rail vehicles for crew access. Rates are based on the agreed schedule with the plant supplier, with a daily hire rate of $4,800 for major machinery and $2,200 for support vehicles.

**3.5 Project Management & Overheads (WCMP-PMO) – $400,000**

This category funds the program management office, including engineering supervision, quality assurance, safety coordination, and administrative support. It also includes the cost of environmental monitoring and community liaison activities associated with the works.

**4. Contingency**

The Western Corridor Maintenance Program total_budget_aud is 4800000 AUD. Record status: current.

The contingency reserve of $500,000 is held centrally and may only be accessed with the written approval of the Program Director. The reserve is intended to cover cost variations arising from:

- Unforeseen ground conditions or discovery of unrecorded services;
- Weather-related delays and associated extension of plant hire periods;
- Variations to the scope of works requested by MetroTrack Rail Services;
- Price escalation on key materials, where the increase exceeds 5% of the original estimate.

Requests for contingency funding must be submitted using the standard variation form and must include a revised cost estimate and justification. The Program Director will assess each request against the available balance and the overall program risk profile.

**5. Approval Authority**

The following financial delegation limits apply to all WCMP expenditure:

| Role | Approval Limit ($) |
|---|---|
| Program Director | 250,000 |
| Senior Project Engineer | 75,000 |
| Project Engineer | 25,000 |
| Contracts Administrator | 10,000 |

All expenditures above the Program Director's limit of $250,000 require the prior written approval of the General Manager, Infrastructure Delivery, MetroTrack Rail Services. This approval must be obtained before any commitment is made, including the placement of purchase orders or the execution of contracts.

For expenditure above $500,000, approval must also be obtained from the Chief Financial Officer, and the expenditure must be included in the monthly financial report to the Board.

**6. Budget Management and Reporting**

The program management office will maintain a detailed budget register, updated weekly, recording all commitments and expenditures against each category code. Monthly financial reports will be provided to the Program Director and the General Manager, Infrastructure Delivery, showing actual expenditure against budget, projected outturn, and any variances requiring explanation.
**7. Cost Breakdown by Category**

The approved program budget is allocated across the following cost categories. All figures are exclusive of GST and are drawn against the budget codes identified in the budget register.

| Category Code | Description | Allocation ($) |
|---|---|---|
| WCMP-100 | Track access charges | 1,150,000 |
| WCMP-200 | Labour – direct and indirect | 1,650,000 |
| WCMP-300 | Materials and consumables | 820,000 |
| WCMP-400 | Plant and equipment hire | 480,000 |
| WCMP-500 | Contractor payments | 350,000 |
| WCMP-600 | Survey, design and testing | 190,000 |
| WCMP-700 | Project management and administration | 160,000 |
| WCMP-800 | Environmental and heritage compliance | 200,000 |
| | **Total category allocations** | **5,000,000** |

The difference between the total category allocations and the approved program budget of $4,800,000 is accounted for by an anticipated recoverable adjustment relating to the finalisation of the track access agreement for the Northbridge Junction possession in February 2026. This adjustment has been reviewed by the Contracts Administrator and is expected to be credited against the WCMP-100 category before the end of the financial year. Should the adjustment not be realised, the Program Director will reallocate funds from the contingency reserve in accordance with clause 4 of this memo.

**7.1 Track Access Charges**

Track access charges are calculated at a protected rate of $2,500 per hour of possession time, as specified in the current Network Access Agreement. This rate has been applied consistently across all planned possessions, including night works, which are also charged at the $2,500 per hour rate. The allocation under WCMP-100 assumes a total of 460 possession hours across the program, comprising:

- Day possessions (Monday to Friday, 09:00–15:00): 280 hours
- Night possessions (Monday to Thursday, 22:00–05:00): 120 hours
- Weekend possessions (Saturday and Sunday, 07:00–19:00): 60 hours

The track access charge is a fixed cost per hour and is not subject to escalation during the program. Any variation to the planned possession hours must be requested through the standard variation process and will be assessed against the WCMP-100 allocation. If additional possession hours are required, the associated access charges must be funded from the contingency reserve or through an approved variation to the program budget.

**7.2 Labour**

The labour allocation of $1,650,000 covers direct employment costs for MetroTrack Rail Services staff and contracted labour engaged under the enterprise agreement. The allocation is based on the following assumed staffing profile:

| Role | Daily Rate ($) | Estimated Days | Subtotal ($) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Track maintenance workers (gang of 8) | 3,200 | 210 | 672,000 |
| Machine operators | 1,100 | 180 | 198,000 |
| Lookouts and protection officers | 850 | 210 | 178,500 |
| Signallers (for possessions) | 950 | 120 | 114,000 |
| Supervisors | 1,300 | 160 | 208,000 |
| Surveyors | 1,050 | 60 | 63,000 |
| Administration and planning support | 700 | 180 | 126,000 |
| **Total labour** | | | **1,559,500** |

The remaining $90,500 under WCMP-200 is held as a labour contingency to cover overtime, shift penalties, and unplanned call-outs. Overtime is payable at the rates prescribed in the enterprise agreement, and any claim for overtime must be authorised by the Senior Project Engineer before the work is undertaken. The labour allocation assumes a standard working week of Monday to Friday, with night and weekend work scheduled only where required for possession access.

**7.3 Materials and Consumables**

The materials allocation of $820,000 covers the supply and delivery of track components, ballast, fastenings, and other consumables required for the programmed works. The principal material items are:

| Item | Unit | Quantity | Unit Cost ($) | Subtotal ($) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rail – 60 kg/m, heat-treated | tonne | 240 | 1,450 | 348,000 |
| Sleepers – concrete, standard gauge | each | 1,800 | 145 | 261,000 |
| Ballast – crushed rock, nominal 50 mm | tonne | 1,200 | 85 | 102,000 |
| Fastenings – elastic rail clips and baseplates | set | 3,600 | 18 | 64,800 |
| Welding consumables and thermite kits | each | 120 | 240 | 28,800 |
| Lubricants and track oils | litre | 800 | 12 | 9,600 |
| Signage and temporary warning devices | lot | 20 | 300 | 6,000 |
| **Total materials** | | | | **820,200** |

I refer to your application dated 12 December 2025, and subsequent correspondence, seeking regulatory approval for the safety compliance arrangements proposed for the 2026 WCMP works season. This letter constitutes the Rail Safety Regulation Unit's formal approval of the programme, subject to the conditions outlined below and in the attached schedule.

The approval covers all planned track maintenance, renewal, and associated civil works activities along the West Corridor line between Corinda and Ipswich, including the branch to Rosewood, for the period 1 February 2026 to 30 April 2026. The programme comprises 47 discrete work packages, of which 31 are classified as low-risk, 12 as medium-risk, and 4 as high-risk under the Risk Classification Framework (RCF) version 4.2.

**1. APPROVAL SUMMARY**

The RSRU has assessed the Safety Compliance Programme (SCP) submitted by MetroTrack, together with the supporting risk assessments, environmental management plans, and community engagement strategies. Following a review of the documentation and consultation with relevant stakeholders, the RSRU approves the SCP with effect from 1 February 2026, subject to the conditions set out in this letter and the attached schedule.

This approval supersedes the interim approval granted on 8 January 2026 (reference RSRU-WCMP-2026-0087) and remains in force until 30 April 2026, or until the completion of all approved works, whichever occurs first. **2.1 Possession and Isolation Management.** All works requiring possession of the track must be conducted under a valid possession authority. MetroTrack must ensure that no works commence without a current possession authority issued by the Network Control Centre, and that all possession limits are clearly marked and communicated to all personnel on site. The possession authority must remain in force for the duration of the work activity, and any extension or variation must be recorded and approved in accordance with the Network Rules.

**2.2 Lookout and Warning Systems.** For all works conducted under absolute or modified track occupancy, MetroTrack must implement an appropriate lookout system. This includes high-visibility clothing, safety helmets, safety footwear, and any additional PPE identified in the specific risk assessment for each task. MetroTrack must ensure that PPE is inspected regularly and replaced where damaged or no longer fit for purpose.

This includes measures to protect water quality in the Oxley Creek catchment, manage spoil and waste materials, control dust and noise, and protect native vegetation along the corridor. Any environmental incident, including any unauthorised discharge, spill, or disturbance to protected vegetation, must be reported to the RSRU within two hours of detection.

2. **Delegated Expenditure Authority:** Consistent with the MetroTrack Delegation Matrix current as at the date of this approval, the authorised signatory ceiling for the Program Director, WCMP, is 200,000 AUD. Any single expenditure commitment or contract variation exceeding this ceiling, or the aggregate of related commitments exceeding this ceiling in any financial quarter, must be referred to the MetroTrack Executive General Manager, Infrastructure Delivery, for approval prior to commitment. This condition is intended to ensure that financial authorisations remain proportionate to the risk profile of the works and are subject to appropriate governance oversight.

3. **Safety Waiver Conditions:** Where the SCS identifies a departure from a prescriptive requirement of the Code, the associated safety waiver (reference numbers WCMP/SW/2025/001 through WCMP/SW/2025/014) shall remain in effect only for the duration and scope specified in each waiver. Each waiver must be revalidated by the MetroTrack Safety Assurance Manager no later than 21 days prior to the commencement of any works to which the waiver applies. A register of current waivers, including effective dates and expiry dates, shall be maintained and made available to the Department upon request.

4. **Interface Coordination:** MetroTrack shall ensure that all maintenance activities are coordinated with the relevant rail operator (Queensland Rail) and any third-party contractors through the established Interface Coordination Forum. Minutes of the forum shall be retained and provided to the Department within ten (10) business days of each meeting.

5. **Reporting of Significant Incidents:** In accordance with section 48 of the Regulation, any incident or near miss arising from WCMP activities that results in, or has the potential to result in, injury to persons, damage to infrastructure, or a significant disruption to rail services must be reported to the Department’s Rail Safety Regulation Unit within two (2) hours of the incident being identified. A written report must follow within five (5) business days.

6. **Periodic Review:** This approval shall be reviewed by the Department at intervals not exceeding twelve (12) months from the date of issue, or earlier if there is a material change to the scope, risk profile, or key personnel associated with the WCMP.

Dear Mr. Okafor,

**RE: APPROVAL OF SAFETY COMPLIANCE PROGRAMME – WEST CORRIDOR MAINTENANCE PROGRAMME (WCMP), 2026 WORKS SEASON**

I refer to your application dated 12 December 2025, and subsequent correspondence, seeking regulatory approval for the safety compliance arrangements proposed for the 2026 WCMP works season. This letter constitutes the Rail Safety Regulation Unit's formal approval of the programme, subject to the conditions outlined below and in the attached schedule.

The approval covers all planned track maintenance, renewal, and associated civil works activities along the West Corridor line between Corinda and Ipswich, including the branch to Rosewood, for the period 1 February 2026 to 30 April 2026. The programme comprises 47 discrete work packages, of which 31 are classified as low-risk, 12 as medium-risk, and 4 as high-risk under the Risk Classification Framework (RCF) version 4.2.

**1. APPROVAL SUMMARY**

The RSRU has assessed the Safety Compliance Programme (SCP) submitted by MetroTrack, together with the supporting risk assessments, environmental management plans, and community engagement strategies. Following a review of the documentation and consultation with relevant stakeholders, the RSRU approves the SCP with effect from 1 February 2026, subject to the conditions set out in this letter and the attached schedule.

This approval supersedes the interim approval granted on 8 January 2026 (reference RSRU-WCMP-2026-0087) and remains in force until 30 April 2026, or until the completion of all approved works, whichever occurs first. Any works not completed by 30 April 2026 will require a separate application for an extension of this approval.

**2. KEY CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL**

The following conditions are considered critical to the safe delivery of the programme. MetroTrack must implement each condition in full and maintain verifiable records of compliance.

**2.1 Possession and Isolation Management.** All works requiring possession of the track must be conducted under a valid possession authority. MetroTrack must ensure that no works commence without a current possession authority issued by the Network Control Centre, and that all possession limits are clearly marked and communicated to all personnel on site. The possession authority must remain in force for the duration of the work activity, and any extension or variation must be recorded and approved in accordance with the Network Rules.

**2.2 Lookout and Warning Systems.** For all works conducted under absolute or modified track occupancy, MetroTrack must implement an appropriate lookout system. This includes the deployment of qualified lookouts at all identified locations, the use of audible and visual warning devices, and the maintenance of a communication link between lookouts and the works supervisor. The lookout system must be tested and confirmed operational prior to the commencement of each work activity.

**2.3 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).** All personnel engaged in works under this approval must wear the prescribed PPE as detailed in the WCMP Safety Compliance Programme. This includes high-visibility clothing, safety helmets, safety footwear, and any additional PPE identified in the specific risk assessment for each task. MetroTrack must ensure that PPE is inspected regularly and replaced where damaged or no longer fit for purpose.

**2.4 Environmental Management.** MetroTrack must implement the environmental management measures identified in the Environmental Management Plan (EMP) submitted with the application. This includes measures to protect water quality in the Oxley Creek catchment, manage spoil and waste materials, control dust and noise, and protect native vegetation along the corridor. Any environmental incident, including any unauthorised discharge, spill, or disturbance to protected vegetation, must be reported to the RSRU within two hours of detection.
